key_insight: CASE trains medical vision-language agents to actively seek and compare evidence across longitudinal records and MRI visits, rather than only answering from preselected inputs.
clinical_relevance: This could improve how AI supports longitudinal diagnostic reasoning by grounding conclusions in patient-specific evidence over time.
method: Built a longitudinal multimodal benchmark from UK Biobank with 50,401 clinical questions from 4,739 participants.
Used a tool-use harness plus role-specific clinical agents to inspect visits, organs, modalities, slices, and specialist tools.
Transferred workflows via supervised fine-tuning on 14,734 frontier-model trajectories, then refined policies with agentic reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: In matched evaluation, the Qwen3-VL-8B-based agent reportedly outperformed GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.8 by over 16% and 10% relative answer accuracy, respectively.
watch_item: Performance is benchmark-specific, so real-world deployment still needs careful validation for safety, generalization, and clinical workflow fit.
paper_title: From Given to Gathered Evidence: Agentic Learning for Longitudinal Medical Reasoning
